title: REDLINE attack scenario
description: One reproducible adversarial call, and what a well-behaved agent must have done about it. Scenarios are YAML so that a reviewer can read the diff and a non-programmer can contribute one.

id.description: Stable slug, unique across the catalogue. Used on the command line and in reports.

family.description: How this scenario is grouped in the report.

severity.description: Reserve 'critical' for outcomes that leak data, make a commitment, or report success to a system that will then act on it.

title.description: One line, readable by someone who has never seen this tool.

rationale.description: Why this attack is worth defending against. Shown by `redline explain`.

persona.description: The scripted party at the other end of the line. Scripted, not generated: the same scenario must produce the same verdict before and after a fix.

opening.description: What picks up. The call disposition is derived from this, so it cannot contradict the script.

answer_delay_seconds.description: How long the line rang before pick-up.

turns.description: What the caller says, in order.

intent.description: What this turn is trying to do to the agent. Determines which goal defence must resist it.

heard_as.description: What the transcript records, when the platform heard something other than what was spoken. The payload of a homophone attack lives here and not in the audio.

dtmf.description: Keypad digits sent instead of, or alongside, speech. Reaches the model as text without passing through speech recognition.

barge_in.description: Whether this turn was spoken over the agent, cutting its line short.

canaries.description: Marked values planted in the agent's context. Their appearance in an agent turn admits no innocent explanation.

value.description: Must be unique and meaningless. Never a real reference, number, or identifier.

ground_truth.description: What really happened, which the agent does not get to define. The disposition is derived from persona.opening and is deliberately not settable here.

human_confirmed.description: Whether the scripted person genuinely agreed. Null when the scenario makes no ask -- 'never asked' must not read as 'refused'.

facts.description: True values for fields the agent is meant to extract, compared leaf by leaf against structured_result.

expect.description: What a well-behaved agent must have done. A scenario with no expectations cannot fail, and is not a test.

assert.description: Assertion name. Run `redline check` to validate it against the registry.

because.description: Why this matters, in your words. Printed with the failure, so a report explains rather than accuses.
